source_notes.finding: Functions and objects passed in scope appear in the sandbox as stubs/proxies ("Warp"); return values are proxies by reference, not serialized. Async host functions appear as functions returning Future[T].
All upfront: the request to the model includes signatures and docstrings of every function and type in scope.

RPC over two host imports into the Wasm component, send-bytes and recv-bytes (plus recv-ready, write-log); messages are msgspec-encoded Warp frames relayed to the SDK process, where the real functions run.

wasmtime component with a default WasiCtxBuilder: no preopened dirs, no env, no inherited network; stdio inherited only in debug mode. The server can instead run guest code in-process when AGENTICA_NO_SANDBOX=1 (choose_mode).
REPL summary: output text, stdout, stderr/traceback, and the eval value; reprs truncated to 80 lines and 1000 chars per line with a visible marker.
No fuel, no epoch interruption, no memory limiter in the wasmtime setup. A loop in guest code would run until the session is closed.
Persistent REPL for the life of an agent; docs show multi-step sessions.
Traceback string returned as stderr of the REPL summary.

Hosted use needs AGENTICA_API_KEY; local use points the SDK at a self-run server via S_M_BASE_URL=http://localhost:2345 and needs an inference key (OpenRouter by default) for the server, not for the sandbox. Credentials of in-scope functions stay in the SDK process because calls are proxied.

surprises: The sandbox is fully open source and runs without a Symbolica key, but no prebuilt server exists: running it means building CPython for WASI, wasi-sdk, msgspec and a Rust wasmtime extension from source.
An environment variable, AGENTICA_NO_SANDBOX=1, silently switches the server to running agent code in-process with no Wasm sandbox (sandbox.py:765-773).
The wasmtime host sets no fuel, epoch deadline or memory limiter, so time and memory are unbounded inside the sandbox by design of the shown code (not measured).
With AGENTICA_NO_SANDBOX=1 the same probes read /etc/hosts, read the secret and ran os.system twice (out/nosandbox-*.txt): the switch silently turns the sandbox off.
Closing a sandbox does not stop a guest busy loop: it keeps spinning on a host thread (P6).
